title: Collection of Kabbalah and Hekhalot texts (MS. Michael 9)
shelf_note: A medieval Hebrew manuscript leaf of Sefer Yetzirah (twelve simple letters, zodiac, months). It matches the title and the language. The record has no tradition or collections, so there is nothing to contradict.
structure_note: The counts disagree with each other: structure.pages_translated is 0, but pages_translated_field is 359. One of these instruments is wrong (E2). Only 165 of 388 pages have a printed number, with 21 backsteps and 14 repeats. On a manuscript foliated in pencil ("8" on this leaf) that pattern points to folio numbers read inconsistently or recto/verso sharing a folio number, not a scan splice. One page cannot settle it.

pages.layout: single column of 18 lines in Hebrew semi-cursive; pencil folio '8' top left; a strip of the facing leaf at the right edge; ruler at the left

other.note: The summary and keywords describe 'twelve leaders in the soul' and the organ lists as the page's content. Derived metadata is built on the invented lines

missing.english: Twelve simple letters: they are half
missing.why: 'Simple letters' is the Sefer Yetzirah class of the twelve letters that are neither 'mothers' nor 'doubles'. Without a note, and without being told the text is Sefer Yetzirah, the reader cannot follow it
'Springs' (eyes/nostrils) and 'devourers' (organs that grind food) are opaque terms for parts of the body and are left unexplained
המיות (the 'murmuring' organs, usually the intestines) is unexplained

book_verdict: The leaf is a real Sefer Yetzirah passage, but about a third of the transcription is invented or recited from memory (the battle formula, a Deuteronomy verse, wrong numerals, seven month names dropped). The fluent English carries all of it, along with a wrong 'divine name' gloss. An expert would flag the page on sight.
